experiment_design.technical_details: This study designs a comparative Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA) and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) framework to test the hypothesis that universal recycling of complex composites is economically infeasible without internalized externalities. The core technical challenge is quantifying the 'entropy cost' of separation for multi-layer materials (e.g., diaper components: plastic, cellulose, superabsorbent polymers) versus single-stream materials. The model will calculate the Net Present Value (NPV) and Energy Return on Investment (EROI) for two scenarios: (1) Current Market Conditions (no carbon tax, no subsidy for recycled content), and (2) Internalized Externalities (including social cost of carbon and avoided landfill health costs). The falsification condition is met if Scenario 1 yields NPV > 0 and EROI > 1 for representative complex waste streams.

source.name: Global Waste Composition and Recycling Rates Database
source.description: Aggregated municipal waste reports providing baseline composition data for complex waste streams (diapers, cigarette butts, multi-layer packaging) and current recycling rates.

target.name: Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) Data for Composite Materials
target.description: Process-specific energy input, chemical usage, and yield data for mechanical and chemical recycling pathways of composite materials. Includes market price data for virgin vs. recycled outputs.

experiment_design.methods:
1. **System Boundary Definition**: Define cradle-to-gate boundaries for recycling processes of three representative complex composites: (a) Disposable diapers, (b) Cigarette filters, (c) Multi-layer food packaging. 
2. **LCA Modeling**: Use ISO 14040/14044 standards to quantify energy input (MJ/kg) and greenhouse gas emissions (kg CO2e/kg) for separation and reprocessing. 
3. **Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA)**: Construct cash flow models including capital expenditure (CAPEX) for sorting/separation infrastructure, operational expenditure (OPEX) for energy/labor, and revenue from sold recyclates. 
4. **Externality Valuation**: Apply standard social cost of carbon (e.g., $50-100/ton CO2e) and estimated health costs of landfill leachate/microplastics to create an 'adjusted' economic model. 
5. **Sensitivity Analysis**: Vary key parameters (energy price, virgin material price, separation efficiency) to identify break-even points.

baselines: Virgin Material Production Baseline: Cost and energy intensity of producing equivalent virgin materials (e.g., virgin plastic pellets, virgin pulp).
Landfilling/Incineration Baseline: Current disposal costs and associated environmental externalities without recycling.
metrics: Net Present Value (NPV) over 10-year project life
Energy Return on Investment (EROI)
Levelized Cost of Recycling (LCOR) per ton
Break-even Carbon Price required for profitability
experiments.ablation: Compare results with and without: (1) Advanced AI-driven sorting efficiency improvements (simulated +15% purity), (2) Subsidies for recycled content (simulated $200/ton credit), (3) Exclusion of environmental externalities.
experiments.validation_protocol: Cross-validate LCA inventory data against peer-reviewed literature for similar processes. Validate TEA assumptions against industry reports for waste management facility costs. Ensure mass balance closure in all process models.

experiment_design.technical_details: This study designs a comparative Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA) and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) framework to test the hypothesis that universal recycling of complex composites is economically infeasible without internalized externalities. The core technical challenge is quantifying the 'entropy cost' of separation for multi-layer materials (e.g., diaper components: plastic, cellulose, superabsorbent polymers) versus single-stream materials. The model will calculate the Net Present Value (NPV) and Energy Return on Investment (EROI) for two scenarios: (1) Current Market Conditions (no carbon tax, no subsidy for recycled content), and (2) Internalized Externalities (including social cost of carbon and avoided landfill health costs). The falsification condition is met if Scenario 1 yields NPV > 0 and EROI > 1 for representative complex waste streams.

experiment_design.methods:

2. **LCA Modeling**: Use ISO 14040/14044 standards to quantify energy input (MJ/kg) and greenhouse gas emissions (kg CO2e/kg) for separation and reprocessing. 
3. **Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA)**: Construct cash flow models including capital expenditure (CAPEX) for sorting/separation infrastructure, operational expenditure (OPEX) for energy/labor, and revenue from sold recyclates. 
4. **Externality Valuation**: Apply standard social cost of carbon (e.g., $50-100/ton CO2e) and estimated health costs of landfill leachate/microplastics to create an 'adjusted' economic model. 
5. **Sensitivity Analysis**: Vary key parameters (energy price, virgin material price, separation efficiency) to identify break-even points.

experiment_design.technical_details: This study designs a comparative Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA) and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) framework to test the hypothesis that universal recycling of complex composites is economically infeasible without internalized externalities. The core technical challenge is quantifying the 'entropy cost' of separation for multi-layer materials (e.g., diaper components: plastic, cellulose, superabsorbent polymers) versus single-stream materials. The model will calculate the Net Present Value (NPV) and Energy Return on Investment (EROI) for two scenarios: (1) Current Market Conditions (no carbon tax, no subsidy for recycled content), and (2) Internalized Externalities (including social cost of carbon and avoided landfill health costs). The falsification condition is met if Scenario 1 yields NPV > 0 and EROI > 1 for representative complex waste streams.

experiment_design.methods:
1. **System Boundary Definition**: Define cradle-to-gate boundaries for recycling processes of three representative complex composites: (a) Disposable diapers, (b) Cigarette filters, (c) Multi-layer food packaging. 
2. **LCA Modeling**: Use ISO 14040/14044 standards to quantify energy input (MJ/kg) and greenhouse gas emissions (kg CO2e/kg) for separation and reprocessing. 
3. **Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA)**: Construct cash flow models including capital expenditure (CAPEX) for sorting/separation infrastructure, operational expenditure (OPEX) for energy/labor, and revenue from sold recyclates. 
4. **Externality Valuation**: Apply standard social cost of carbon (e.g., $50-100/ton CO2e) and estimated health costs of landfill leachate/microplastics to create an 'adjusted' economic model. 
5. **Sensitivity Analysis**: Vary key parameters (energy price, virgin material price, separation efficiency) to identify break-even points.

Landfilling/Incineration Baseline: Current disposal costs and associated environmental externalities without recycling.

Energy Return on Investment (EROI)
Levelized Cost of Recycling (LCOR) per ton
Break-even Carbon Price required for profitability

experiments.validation_protocol: Cross-validate LCA inventory data against peer-reviewed literature for similar processes. Validate TEA assumptions against industry reports for waste management facility costs. Ensure mass balance closure in all process models.
